identity.real_world_identity_notes: Customer GT3 racing car built on the AMG GT platform with the naturally aspirated 6.2 litre V8. The manufacturer specifies a sequential six-speed racing gearbox mounted at the rear axle in transaxle configuration.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: AMG's operation manual requires clutch operation from neutral to first and instructs the driver to ease the clutch in; an exact 2016 first drive identifies the otherwise-hidden clutch pedal as the control racers use to get the car moving.

The simulator drives accepted no-lift upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts because they detected automatic cut or blip. Real-car throttle-lift technique remains open rather than being inferred from simulator behavior.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mercedes-amg-gt3.20260813t160013204z-821a21ab by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: AMS2 1.6.9.91 accepted clutch-free move-off, unlike the original real car's driver-operated clutch launch.

confidence.basis: The guided move-off test directly observed clutch-free pull-away with automatic clutch and shifting assists disabled.
Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world six-speed sequential paddle transmission is established by a registered source.

notes: Observed live in ACC 21257365 via guided verification observation acc.mercedes-amg-gt3-2015.20260823t042452064z-2045406c by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: ACC accepted the guided full-throttle clutchless upshift while the authentic real-car throttle-lift claim remains open.

confidence.basis: Mercedes-AMG establishes the original GT3 and six-speed sequential transmission. ACC reported the original model, GT3 class and stable internal id `mercedes_amg_gt3`; the guided drive directly established simulator behavior and cockpit.

claims.basis: The registered source establishes the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The manufacturer specifies a sequential six-speed racing gearbox in a rear transaxle; the live drive confirmed six paddle gears and clutch-free move-off.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

AMG Customer Sports' operation manual requires clutch operation when selecting first from neutral and tells the driver to ease the clutch in. A first-person test of the exact original 2016 car independently identifies the clutch pedal as the control used to get the car moving. Neither source establishes anti-stall or an automated launch clutch.

Telemetry name `Mercedes AMG GT3 2015`, internal id `mercedes_amg_gt3`, and class `GT3` identify the original car first shown in 2015 and exclude ACC's separately reviewed `mercedes_amg_gt3_evo` 2020 update. The curated year records the 2016 customer-racing debut.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: Whether the car needs a throttle lift on upshifts is not established. A guided drive settles it, by holding the throttle through an upshift and seeing whether the gear engages.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Paddle sequential with one job left for your left foot, which is the clutch to pull away. After that it cuts the upshift and blips the downshift on its own.
